evidence.excerpt:
We present a comparative analysis of six models belonging to Convolutional Neu-
ral Network (CNN), Transformer, and Mamba families for automated eye disease 
classification from fundus images under identical experimental conditions. To the best 
of our knowledge, our work is the first to explore Mamba-based models for auto-
mated multi-class eye disease classification from color fundus images. Our analysis 
suggests that, when evaluated fairly, modern CNN, Transformer, and Mamba-based 
models provide similar performance for eye disease classification on the Eye Disease 
Image Dataset (EDID). Along with analyzing individual model performance, we further 
evaluate performance using a logit-level ensemble of the top three models. The 
ensemble results imply that these model families capture partially complementary 
visual features, resulting in a slight performance gain when combined. In

evidence.excerpt:
To evaluate whether oversampling caused inflated minority-class performance, we conducted an ablation study using 
ConvNeXt-B under three settings: the original imbalanced split, class-weighted cross-entropy, and replication-based 
oversampling (Tables 7 and 8). If oversampling had caused memorization, the heavily replicated minority classes would 
be expected to achieve unusually high accuracy. However, CSCR and MS remained the most difficult classes under over-
sampling, with accuracies of 0.650 and 0.483, respectively, while weighted cross-entropy achieved higher scores on both

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Pairwise McNemar tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction and 1000-sample bootstrap confidence intervals on held-out test predictions.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Micro/macro accuracy, macro F1, and multi-class AUC-ROC computed against ground-truth clinical labels on a held-out test split.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-entropy loss optimized with AdamW on the training split, with best-checkpoint selection based on validation loss.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are carefully bounded and well aligned with empirical results, correctly concluding that modern CNN, Transformer, and hybrid Mamba architectures show comparable overall performance on this benchmark, without declaring an unjustified strict hierarchy among top performers.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The study conducts a sound evaluation incorporating micro/macro accuracy, F1 score, AUC-ROC, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, and Holm-Bonferroni corrected pairwise McNemar significance tests, supplemented by class-wise breakdowns and efficiency analyses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Pairwise McNemar statistical significance tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction and 1000-sample bootstrap confidence intervals on held-out test samples.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Micro/macro accuracy, macro F1, and multi-class AUC-ROC calculated against ground-truth clinical diagnostic labels on a held-out test split.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard cross-entropy loss with AdamW optimization on the training split, with checkpoint selection guided by cross-entropy loss on a separate validation set.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently report key limitations including single-seed training runs due to computational constraints, evaluation restricted to a single dataset (EDID), potential unremoved near-duplicates across splits, and fixed identical classification head configurations.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, standardizing the classification head, preprocessing pipeline, training hyperparameters, and class-balancing strategy across all six architectures. Data partitioning is executed prior to augmentation, and near-duplicate leakage is measured and reported.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a rigorous, well-controlled comparative baseline that addresses past methodological issues (such as post-augmentation splitting) in the literature on EDID. Statistical testing, bootstrap resampling, and ablation analyses provide strong positive scientific evidence.
primary.scoped_contribution: A controlled empirical comparison of six representative vision backbones across CNN, Transformer, and Mamba families (RegNetY, ConvNeXt, DeiT, SwinV2, Vim, and MambaVision) for multi-class eye disease classification on the EDID dataset under standardized data splitting and training protocols.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study offers a rigorous, well-controlled comparative baseline that addresses past methodological issues (such as post-augmentation splitting) in the literature on EDID. Statistical testing, bootstrap resampling, and ablation analyses provide strong positive scientific evidence.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently report key limitations including single-seed training runs due to computational constraints, evaluation restricted to a single dataset (EDID), potential unremoved near-duplicates across splits, and fixed identical classification head configurations.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
